Abu al-'Aliyah said: God's share is spent on the door (ritaj) of the Ka'bah. He also reported that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would take the fifth, put his hand into it, take a handful and set it aside for the Ka'bah, and this was God's share; then he would divide the rest into five parts. It is also said that God's share goes to the public treasury (bayt al-mal).

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Nakha'i, Qatadah and al-Shafi'i said: His words ﴿Indeed, for God is a fifth of it﴾ are an opening phrase (istiftah kalam), as a man says to his slave: "May God free you, and I free you," for the sake of blessing and magnifying the matter. The whole world belongs to God, and God's share and the Messenger's share are one. The Messenger (ﷺ) would divide the fifth into five parts. This is the view al-Zamakhshari cited as a possibility. He said: It may be that the meaning of ﴿for God and for the Messenger﴾ (Al-Anfal: 24) is like His words: ﴿God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ (At-Tawbah: 62). And the meaning of His words ﴿Indeed, for God is a fifth of it﴾ may be: it is part of the right of the fifth that it be offered as a means of drawing near to Him alone. Then He singled out these five from among the ways of drawing near, giving them precedence over others, as in His words: ﴿Gabriel and Michael﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 98). The apparent meaning is that the Messenger, peace be upon him, has a share of the fifth.

Ibn 'Abbas said, as al-Tabari reported: God and the Messenger have no share; his share is for his kinsfolk. The fifth is divided into four parts. A group said: it is returned to the four-fifths. 'Ali said: the imam takes the share of God and His Messenger. The apparent meaning is that he, peace be upon him, had no share of the spoils except one share.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: He, peace be upon him, was specially privileged in three respects regarding the spoils: he had a fifth of the fifth; he had a man's share in the remaining four-fifths; and he had the safi, which he took before the spoils were divided, a mount, a sword, or a female slave. No one after him has a safi, by consensus, except what Abu Thawr said, that the safi belongs to the imam. This is an opinion counted among the anomalous views. End of quote.

A group said: the Messenger (ﷺ) did not leave an inheritance, so his share lapsed. It is also said that his share is held in trust for his kinsfolk, and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz sent it to them. A group said: it belongs to the kinsfolk of the one who holds authority after him. al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it was for the Messenger (ﷺ) during his lifetime, and when he died it was given to the custodian of affairs (wali al-amr) after him. End of quote.

Dhu al-qurba (the kinsfolk) means the kinsfolk of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The apparent meaning is the general sense of his kin. A group said: all of Quraysh are kinsfolk. Abu Hanifah and al-Shafi'i said: they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, who deserve it because of support and assistance, not the Banu 'Abd Shams or the Banu Nawfal. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, 'Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and Ibn 'Abbas said: they are only the Banu Hashim. Mujahid said: the family of Muhammad were not permitted to receive charity, so a share of the fifth was given to them. Ibn 'Abbas said: but our people refused this for us and said: all of Quraysh are kinsfolk. The apparent meaning is that this share remains for the kinsfolk, and that it belongs to both their rich and their poor. Ibn 'Abbas said: it was divided into six: for God and the Messenger two shares, and one share for his relatives, until he died. Then Abu Bakr divided the fifth into three parts, and this was also narrated from 'Umar and those who came after him among the caliphs. It is also reported that Abu Bakr withheld the fifth from the Banu Hashim and said: What is due to you is that your poor be given, your unmarried women be married, and whoever among you has no servant be provided with one. As for your wealthy, they are in the position of the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil); the wealthy person is not given anything from charity, nor is a wealthy orphan. It is reported from Zayd ibn 'Ali: it is not permitted for us to build palaces from it, nor to ride fine horses from it.

Some said: the share of the kinsfolk belongs to the kinsfolk of the caliph. The apparent meaning is that the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer are general terms covering the orphans and needy of the Muslims, and the wayfarer is among them. It is also said that the entire fifth belongs to the kinsfolk. It was said to 'Ali: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and the orphans and the needy﴾. He said: our orphans and our needy. It is reported from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali that they said: the whole verse concerns Quraysh and its needy. The apparent sense of the conjunction requires that the shares be shared equally, so that no one is deprived. This is what al-Shafi'i said, and he said: the imam may give preference to those in greater need, but he must not deprive any category of them. Malik said: the imam may give to the neediest and deprive the others of the categories.

The verse does not address who spends the four-fifths. The apparent meaning is that it is not divided among one who did not take part in the gain. If reinforcements join the fighters before the spoils have been brought into the territory of Islam, then according to Abu Hanifah they are partners with them in it. Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, al-Layth and al-Shafi'i said: they do not share with them.

The apparent meaning is that whoever gains something and fights alone, without the imam's permission, has his gain subject to the fifth. This is the view of al-Thawri and al-Shafi'i. The companions of Abu Hanifah said: it belongs to him alone and is not subject to the fifth. Some of them made a distinction on this. al-Awza'i said: if the imam wishes, he may punish him and deprive him; and if he wishes, he may take the fifth and the rest belongs to him.

The apparent meaning is that His words ﴿that whatever you gain﴾ are addressed to the believers. So no share is given to an unbeliever who attended with the imam's permission and fought. The Muslim slaves are included in the address, so what they gain belongs to their masters. al-Thawri and al-Awza'i said: if the protected non-Muslims (ahl al-dhimmah) are enlisted, they are given a share. Ashhab said: if a man in chains (al-muqayyad) or a dhimmi leaves the army and they gain something, the spoils belong to the army and not to them.

The apparent meaning is that His words ﴿that whatever you gain of anything, indeed for God is a fifth of it﴾ are general, covering everything gained: animals, goods, minerals, land and other things. So all of that is subject to the fifth. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, except for adult men. He said: the imam has the choice regarding them between releasing them as a favour, killing them, or taking them captive. Whoever is taken captive among them is subject to the rule of spoils. Malik said: if the imam sees fit to divide the land, that is correct; or if his judgment leads him not to divide it, he does not divide it.

The apparent meaning is that he takes nothing from the spoils other than the fifth. So the spoils of a slain enemy (salab al-maqtul) are general spoils and are not exclusively for the slayer, unless the commander assigns them to him for killing. This is the view of Malik, Abu Hanifah and al-Thawri. al-Awza'i, al-Layth, al-Shafi'i, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, Abu 'Ubayd, al-Tabari and Ibn al-Mundhir said: the spoils belong to the slayer. Ibn Surayj said: they agreed that whoever kills a captive, a woman, an old man, or finishes off a wounded man, or kills someone whose hands and feet have been cut off, or a fleeing man who poses no threat in his flight, like a bound man, has no right to the spoils of any of these. The disagreement is whether it is a condition that the slayer must be facing the slain and in the battle line, or whether this is not a condition. The evidence for these questions is fully treated in the books of jurisprudence, in the books on points of disagreement, and in the books on the rulings of the Qur'an.

The apparent meaning is that ma is a relative pronoun meaning "that which," and it is the subject of anna. Anna is written joined to ma, though by analogy it should be written separately, as they wrote ﴿Indeed what you are promised is coming﴾ (Al-An'am: 134) separately. The predicate of anna is His words ﴿indeed for God is a fifth of it﴾. The phrase anna li-llahi is in the nominative position as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "So the ruling is that for God..." The fa' (then) has entered this clause which functions as the predicate of anna, just as it entered the predicate of anna in His words: ﴿Indeed those who persecuted the believing men and women and then did not repent, for them is the punishment of hellfire﴾ (Al-Buruj: 10).

al-Zamakhshari said: fa-anna li-llahi is a subject whose predicate is omitted, its estimated form being: "a truth" or "a duty": "indeed for God is a fifth of it." End of quote. This second estimate, "or a duty that indeed for God is a fifth of it," makes anna and its two complements the subject of an omitted predicate, which is His words "a duty."

al-Farra' permitted ma to be conditional and governed by ghanimtum, with the subject of anna being an omitted pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n), its estimated form being innahu. The omission of this pronoun with the heavy anna is, according to Sibawayh, restricted to poetry.

al-Ju'fi reported from Harun from Abu 'Amr: fa-inna li-llahi with a kasrah on the hamzah. Ibn 'Atiyyah reported it from al-Ju'fi from Abu Bakr from 'Asim. This reading is strengthened by the reading of al-Nakha'i: fa-li-llahi khumusahu. al-Hasan and 'Abd al-Warith from Abu 'Amr read khumsahu with a sukun on the mim. al-Nakha'i read khimsahu with a kasrah on the kha', by assimilation (ittiba'), meaning the kha' takes the vowel of what precedes it, as in the reading of one who read (wa-al-sama'i dhati al-hubuk) with a kasrah on the ha', assimilating to the vowel of the ta', disregarding the sakin because it is a weak unprotected sakin.

Consider how fine this construction is: He made the existence of the fifth belong to God alone, and separated His name from the conjunctions by the phrase khumusahu, to make clear that God alone has the entitlement to the fifth. Then He conjoined the others with Him in a subordinate way. The construction could have been: fa-inna li-llahi wa-li-l-rasuli wa-li-dhi al-qurba wa-al-yatama wa-al-masakin wa-ibn al-sabil khumusahu, but it did not come that way.

The conditional's answer is omitted, its estimated form being: if you have believed in God, then know that the fifth of the spoils must be offered as a means of drawing near. Mere knowledge is not meant, but knowledge together with acting upon its requirement. For this reason some estimated: if you have believed in God, then accept what you were commanded regarding the spoils. Whoever held that the condition is connected in meaning to His words ﴿the best Protector and the best Helper﴾ (Al-Anfal: 40) is far off, the estimate being: "then know that God is your protector," with "and what We sent down" conjoined to "in God".

The Day of Discrimination (yawm al-furqan) is the Day of Badr, without disagreement. On it truth was distinguished from falsehood. The two hosts (al-jam'an) are the host of the believers and the host of the unbelievers. In it the chieftains of Quraysh were killed, as stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Miqsam, al-Hasan and Qatadah. It took place on Friday, the seventeenth of Ramadan in the second year after the Hijrah. This is the view of the majority. Abu Salih said it was on the nineteenth day.

What was sent down (al-munzal) refers to the signs, the angels and the victory. He concluded with an attribute of power, because God, exalted is He, granted the believers, though few, victory over the unbelievers, though many, on that day.

Zayd ibn 'Ali read 'ubudina with two dammahs, like the reading of the one who read wa-'ubud al-taghut with two dammahs. According to the reading 'abdina, it refers to the Messenger (ﷺ); according to 'ubudina, it refers to the Messenger and those believers with him.

The accusative of (yawm al-furqan) is that it is an adverbial complement governed by His words (wa-ma anzalna). al-Zajjaj said: it may also be governed by ghanimtum, meaning: that whatever you gained on the Day of Discrimination, the day the two hosts met, then indeed for such-and-such is its fifth; that is, if you have believed in God, so submit to that and comply. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: this interpretation is good in meaning, but there is an objection: it separates the adverb from what it depends on by this long stretch of speech. End of quote.

What al-Zajjaj said is not permissible. If ma is conditional, according to al-Farra's analysis, then the separation of the verb of the condition from its object by the answer clause and its dependents is required. If ma is relative, then it is not permissible to separate the verb of the relative clause from its object by the predicate of anna.

﴿When you were on the near bank of the valley and they were on the far bank, and the caravan was lower than you﴾. al-'Udwah is the bank of the valley; it is also called shafir and daffah. It was named so because it prevents the water in the valley from passing beyond it, that is, it holds it back. The poet said:

"The rushing torrents kept me from visiting her,
and she said: behind her is a fierce, shifting war."

(p. 500) The open plain running alongside the valley is called *'udwa* (the near bank), because it is adjacent to the valley. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read *bil-'idwati* with a kasra on the ʿayn in both occurrences. The rest of the Seven Readers read it with a damma, while al-Hasan, Qatadah, Zayd ibn 'Ali and 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd read it with a fatha. Abu 'Amr denied the damma. Al-Akhfash said that only the kasra has been heard from the Arabs. Abu 'Ubayd said the damma is the most common of the three. Al-Yazidi said the kasra is the dialect of the Hijaz. It is possible that all three are dialectal variants. It is also possible that the fatha is a verbal noun that was used as a name. A line of Aws is also transmitted with both the kasra and the damma:

"A horseman who did not hold his bank today; they turned and fled swiftly, and had no intention of advancing."

It was also read *bil-'idyati*, with the waw changed to a ya' because of the kasra on the ʿayn. They did not count the unvowelled letter as a barrier, because it is a weak barrier. They did the same in *sibyatin*, *qinyatin* and *dinya*, as in their saying, "He is my cousin *dinya*." The basic form in this is the uncorrected one, as in *al-sifwa*, *al-dhirwa* and *al-rib'a*. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud the text is *bil-'udwati al-'ulya* (the upper bank) and *wa-hum bil-'udwati al-sufla* (the lower bank). The valley of Badr, for those facing east and the qibla, lies toward the sea, which is near that region. Al-Madina is in the valley, from the place of the battle, in the east, and the distance between them is two stages of travel. Zayd ibn 'Ali read *al-qusya*, and we have already mentioned that this is the analogical form. It is the dialect of Tamim.

The better view is that *wa-hum* and *wal-rakb* are conjoined to *antum* (you). They are then introductory subjects that divide the description of their state and the state of their enemies. It is also possible that the two waws are the waw of the circumstantial clause (*wawa al-hal*). *Asfala* is an adverbial of place in the position of the predicate. Zayd ibn 'Ali read *asfalu* with a damma, extending the adverb so that it became the subject itself, by metaphor. *Al-rakb* (the caravan) are the forty men who were leading the caravan of Abu Sufyan. It is said they were the camels carrying the provisions and goods of the unbelievers, which were in a place they felt safe.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask, what is the benefit of this specification, and of mentioning the positions of the two groups, and that the caravan was lower than them? I say: the benefit is to inform about a state that indicates the strength of the enemy's position and its might, the completeness of its numbers, and the ready means of victory for it. It also shows the weakness of the Muslims' position and the scattering of their affairs. It shows that their victory in such a state was nothing but a work of God, Exalted, and a proof that this matter could not have been accomplished except by His power, His might and His overwhelming ability. The far bank, where the polytheists encamped, had water and was good ground. There was no water on the near bank; it was soft ground, where the feet sink, and one could not walk there except with exhaustion and hardship. The caravan was behind the backs of the enemy, despite their large numbers. Protecting it strengthened their zeal and sharpened their intentions in fighting for it. For this reason the Arabs used to go out to war with their women and wealth, so that the defence of the sanctities and their jealousy for them would move them to exert their utmost effort in battle, so that they would not leave behind them anything they might think of withdrawing to. This gathers their hearts, controls their resolve, settles their souls on not leaving their positions and not abandoning their stations, and on spending the utmost of their valour and the extreme of their strength. In it is a depiction of what God, Glorified is He, arranged regarding the affair of the battle of Badr." End of quotation. It is an excellent statement.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "The caravan and the one who managed its affair, Abu Sufyan, had turned aside from Badr when he learned of the Prophet ﷺ, and took the route of the sea. So it was lower in relation to the upper part of the valley from where [the Prophet's army] came."

﴿And if you had made an appointment with one another, you would have differed about the appointment; but [it was so] that God might accomplish a matter that was to be done, so that whoever perished might perish by clear proof, and whoever lived might live by clear proof. Indeed God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

The meeting took place without an appointment. Mujahid said: "Abu Sufyan and his companions came from Syria as merchants, and they did not perceive the companions of Badr. The companions of Muhammad ﷺ did not perceive the unbelievers of Quraysh, nor did the unbelievers of Quraysh perceive Muhammad ﷺ and his companions, until they met at the water of Badr, all of them to draw water, and they fought. The companions of Muhammad ﷺ overcame them and took them captive." Al-Tabari and others said: the meaning is, if you had agreed on a meeting in order to gather, then had known their numbers and your own scarcity, you would have differed and not gathered with them. Al-Zamakhshari said the same. He said: "If you and the people of Mecca had made an appointment and agreed among yourselves on a time to meet for battle, some of you would have feared others. Your scarcity and their abundance would have deterred you from keeping the appointment, and what was in their hearts of awe of the Messenger of God ﷺ and the Muslims would have deterred them too. So there would not have come about for you the meeting that God had enabled and arranged for." Al-Mahdawi said: the meaning is that you would have differed because of the hindrances and obstacles that block people.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "This is nobler than the view of al-Tabari, and sounder." Its explanation is that the purpose of the verse is to make clear God's blessing and power in the story of Badr and His facilitating of what was facilitated of it. So the meaning is: when God prepared this situation for you, if you had made an appointment for it, you would have differed, except with God's facilitation, which completed it. This is like when you say to your companion about a matter God willed without much effort: "If we had persisted in this and striven for it, it would not have been accomplished like this."

(p. 501) Al-Kirmani said: "If you and the polytheists had made an appointment for fighting, you would have differed about the appointment, meaning they would not have believed in your agreement, seeking to catch you unawares and to trick you." It is also said: the meaning is, if you had made an appointment apart from God's decree regarding the matter of war, you would have differed about the appointment, because when God does not decree a matter it does not happen. End of quotation.

﴿But [it was so] that God might accomplish﴾: but you met without an appointment, so that God might accomplish a matter of the victory of His religion, the exaltation of His word, and the breaking and humiliation of the unbelievers, which was to be done, meaning established, realised and occurring. He expressed it with *maf'ulan* (to be done) to affirm that it would certainly happen. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "[God] accomplishes a matter which He had decreed in eternity as something to be done for you, on condition that you exist at the time of its existence. All of this is known to Him." Al-Zamakhshari said: *li-yaqdiya Allah* is connected to a deleted element, meaning: so that God might accomplish a matter that had to be done, namely the granting of victory to His friends and the subjugation of His enemies. He arranged this. It is also said: *kana* here means *sara* (became). *Li-yuhlika* is a substitute for *li-yaqdiya*, so it is connected to what *li-yaqdiya* is connected to. It is also said: it is connected to *maf'ulan*. It is also said: the original is *wa-li-yuhlika*, and the conjunction was deleted.

The apparent meaning is: that those among the unbelievers of Quraysh and others who were killed should be destroyed by a clear proof from God and a warning through the message, and that whoever lived should live by a clear proof from Him and a warning, with no argument against him. Ibn Ishaq and others said: *li-yakfura wa-yu'mina* (so that he who disbelieves may disbelieve and he who believes may believe). The meaning is that God, Exalted, made the story of Badr a lesson and a sign, so that whoever believed would believe on the basis of clarity and proof, and whoever disbelieved would disbelieve on the same basis.

Al-A'mash and 'Isma ibn Abi Bakr from 'Asim read *li-yahlika* with a fatha on the lam. Nafi', al-Bazzi and Abu Bakr read *man hayya* with *fakk* (separating the two identical letters), while the rest of the Seven read it with idgham (assimilation). Al-Mutalammis said:

"So this is the time of display, its sharp edge alive."

The separated and the assimilated forms are two well-known dialects. He concluded with these two attributes because disbelief and belief entail verbal utterance and inner conviction. So He is All-Hearing of your words and All-Knowing of your intentions.

﴿When God showed them to you in your dream as few. And had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart and disputed about the matter, but God saved [you]. Indeed He knows what is within the breasts.﴾

The address is to the Messenger ﷺ. The reports are consistent that it was a dream of sleep, in which the Messenger ﷺ saw the unbelievers as few. He informed his companions of it, and their souls were strengthened and they became bold against their enemies. When the Prophet ﷺ awoke he said to his companions: "Rejoice, for I saw the places where the people will fall." The meaning of "few" here is few in worth, weakness and valour, and that they would be defeated and slain. It is not to be taken as few in number, because his dream was true. He knew that they were between nine hundred and a thousand, so it is not possible to interpret it as fewness of numbers.

It is reported from al-Hasan that the meaning of *fi manamika* (in your dream) is *fi 'aynika* (in your eye), because the eye is the place of sleep, just as a coverlet is called a *manama* because one sleeps in it. Thus the seeing would be in waking. On this basis al-Naqqash interpreted it, and he mentioned it from al-Mazini. But what is reported from al-Hasan is weak. Al-Zamakhshari said: "This is an interpretation with forced strain. I do not think the report from al-Hasan is sound, nor does it accord with his knowledge of the language of the Arabs and their eloquence. The meaning is: had He shown them to you as many in your dream, you would have lost heart, meaning you would have been cowardly and shrunk from the encounter, and you would have disputed about the matter, meaning your opinions would have been divided over the question of fighting. That would have been a cause of your defeat and of your not advancing against your enemies, for if he had seen them as many, he would have informed you of his vision, and you would have lost heart. Since the Messenger, peace be upon him, was protected from cowardice and preserved from defects, He attributed the cowardice to those in whom it is possible. So He, Exalted, said: 'you would have lost heart.' This is one of the excellences of the Qur'an. But God saved [you] from cowardice, dispute and disagreement by showing him the unbelievers as few, so he informed them of that, and their souls were strengthened by it. Indeed He knows what is within the breasts, knowing what will be in them of boldness and cowardice, patience and despair." (p. 502)

*Idh* (when) is a substitute for *idh* (the earlier one), and *qalilan* is in the accusative. Al-Zamakhshari said: "[*qalilan* is] a circumstantial accusative (*'ala al-hal*)." What he said is apparent, because *ara* (to show) is a causative form of *ra'a* in the sense of seeing with the eye. It takes two objects: the first is the *kaf* of address to the Messenger ﷺ, and the second is the pronoun for the unbelievers. Thus *qalilan* and *kathiran* are accusatives of circumstance. Some grammarians claimed that *ara* in the sense of seeing in a dream takes three objects, like *a'lama* (to inform), and they took this verse as an example: *idh yurikahum Allah fi manamika qalilan*. On this view, *qalilan* is a third object. But the permissibility of deleting this accusative on its own refutes this view. You say: "I saw Zayd in the sleep," and "God showed me Zayd in the sleep."

﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and made you appear few in their eyes, so that God might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to God all affairs are returned.﴾

This sight was in waking, not in sleep. He made the unbelievers appear few in the eyes of the believers, to belittle them and so that they would not be cowardly in meeting them. Ibn Mas'ud said: "They were made to seem few in our eyes, until I said to a man beside me: do you think they are seventy?" He said: "I think they are a hundred." This was from 'Abd Allah because he had not heard what the Messenger ﷺ was informed of regarding their number.

The believers were made to appear few in the eyes of the unbelievers, to the extent that one of them said: "They are only camel-eaters." This was before the encounter, so that they would be emboldened against the believers and the battle would begin and the fighting would engage. For if they had been numerous before the encounter, they would have held back and sought an escape, or prepared and sought help. When the fighting engaged, God made the believers appear numerous in the eyes of the unbelievers, so they were stunned, awed, their strength failed, and they saw what was not in their reckoning. This is as He said: ﴿They saw them as twice their number with their own eyes﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:13]. The greatest proof against them is the clarity of the sign: its smallness at first and its largeness at the end.

The seeing of each of the two groups by the other could be either because God concealed some of them from others, or because He created in their eyes what made them consider the many as few. This applies if the seeing is literal. If it is in the sense of estimation and the caution that people use, then it is possible. In either case, the Messenger does not fall under the address *idh yurikumuhum* (when He showed them to you), because it is not permissible that he should see the many as few, neither literally nor by estimation. It is possible that it is from the category of belittling the rank, awe and valour, not from the category of belittling the number. Do you not see the saying: "A man is many with his brother"? And the line of the poet:

"I go about and set out in folly, making many of him whom I have little of."

فَهَذا مِن بابِ التَّقْلِيلِ والتَّكْثِيرِ في المَنزِلَةِ والقَدْرِ، لا مِن بابِ تَقْلِيلِ العَدَدِ، لِيَقْضِيَ: أيْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ لِيَقْضِيَ، والمَفْعُولُ في الآيَتَيْنِ هو القِصَّةُ بِأسْرِها؛ وقِيلَ: هُما لِمَعْنَيَيْنِ مِن مَعانِي القِصَّةِ، أُرِيدَ بِالأوَّلِ الوَعْدُ بِالنُّصْرَةِ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ، وبِالثّانِي الِاسْتِمْرارُ عَلَيْها، وتَقَدَّمَ تَفْسِيرُ: ﴿وإلى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ﴾ واخْتِلافُ القُرّاءِ في (تُرْجَعُ) في سُورَةِ البَقَرَةِ.

﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً فاثْبُتُوا واذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا لَعَلَّكم تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ (O you who believe, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much, so that you may prosper). أيْ: فِئَةً كافِرَةً، حَذَفَ الوَصْفَ لِأنَّ المُؤْمِنِينَ ما كانُوا يَلْقَوْنَ إلّا الكُفّارَ، واللِّقاءُ اسْمٌ لِلْقِتالِ غالِبٌ، وأمَرَهم تَعالى بِالثَّباتِ وهو مُقَيَّدٌ بِآيَةِ الضَّعْفِ، وفي الحَدِيثِ (ḥadīth, a prophetic report): «لا تَتَمَنَّوْا لِقاءَ العَدُوِّ وسَلُوا اللَّهَ العافِيَةَ، فَإذا لَقِيتُمُوهم فاثْبُتُوا» . وأمَرَهم بِذِكْرِهِ تَعالى كَثِيرًا في هَذا المَوْطِنِ العَظِيمِ مِن (p-٥٠٣)مُصابَرَةِ العَدُوِّ والتَّلاحُمِ بِالرِّماحِ وبِالسُّيُوفِ، وهي حالَةٌ يَقَعُ فِيها الذُّهُولُ عَنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَأُمِرُوا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ؛ إذْ هو تَعالى الَّذِي يُفْزَعُ إلَيْهِ عِنْدَ الشَّدائِدِ ويُسْتَأْنَسُ بِذِكْرِهِ ويُسْتَنْصَرُ بِدُعائِهِ، ومَن كانَ كَثِيرَ التَّعَلُّقِ بِاللَّهِ ذَكَرَهُ في كُلِّ مَوْطِنٍ حَتّى في المَواضِعِ الَّتِي يُذْهَلُ فِيها عَنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ ويَغِيبُ فِيها الحِسُّ: ﴿ألا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ القُلُوبُ﴾ (Indeed, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest) [al-Ra'd: 28]. وحَكى لِي بَعْضُ الشُّجْعانِ أنَّهُ حالَةَ التِحامِ القِتالِ تَأْخُذُ الشُّجاعَ هِزَّةٌ وتَعْتَرِيهِ، مِثْلَ السُّكْرِ لِهَوْلِ المُلْتَقى، فَأمَرَ المُؤْمِنِينَ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ في هَذِهِ الحالَةِ العَظِيمَةِ، وقَدْ نَظَمَ الشُّعَراءُ هَذا المَعْنى فَذَكَرُوا أنَّهم في أشَقِّ الأوْقاتِ عَلَيْهِمْ وأشَدِّها لَمْ يَنْسَوْا مَحْبُوبَهم وأكْثَرُوا في ذَلِكَ، فَقالَ بَعْضُهم:
؎ذَكَرْتُ سُلَيْمى وحَرُّ الوَغى ∗∗∗ كَقَلْبِيَ ساعَةَ فارَقْتُها
؎وأبْصَرْتُ بَيْنَ القَنا قَدَّها ∗∗∗ وقَدْ مِلْنَ نَحْوِي فَعانَقْتُها
قالَ قَتادَةُ: افْتَرَضَ اللَّهُ ذِكْرَهُ أشْغَلَ ما يَكُونُ العَبْدُ عِنْدَ الضِّرابِ والسُّيُوفِ، وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ (al-Zamakhshari): فِيهِ إشْعارٌ بِأنَّ عَلى العَبْدِ أنْ لا يَفْتُرَ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أشْغَلَ ما يَكُونُ قَلْبًا وأكْثَرَ ما يَكُونُ هَمًّا، وأنْ يَكُونَ نَفْسُهُ مُجْتَمِعَةً لِذَلِكَ وإنْ كانَتْ مُتَوَزِّعَةً عَنْ غَيْرِهِ، وذَكَرَ أنَّ الثَّباتَ وذِكْرَ اللَّهِ سَبَبا الفَلاحِ، وهو الظَّفَرُ بِالعَدُوِّ في الدُّنْيا والفَوْزُ في الآخِرَةِ بِالثَّوابِ، والظّاهِرُ أنَّ الذِّكْرَ المَأْمُورَ بِهِ هو بِاللِّسانِ، فَأمَرَ بِالثَّباتِ بِالجَنانِ وبِالذِّكْرِ بِاللِّسانِ، والظّاهِرُ أنْ لا يُعَيَّنَ ذِكْرٌ؛ وقِيلَ: هو قَوْلُ المُجاهِدِينَ: اللَّهُ أكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أكْبَرُ عِنْدَ لِقاءِ الكُفّارِ؛ وقِيلَ: الدُّعاءُ عَلَيْهِمُ: اللَّهُمَّ اخْذُلْهُمُ، اللَّهُمَّ دَمِّرْهم، وشَبَهُهُ؛ وقِيلَ: دُعاءُ المُؤْمِنِينَ؛ لِأنْفُسِهِمْ بِالنَّصْرِ والظَّفَرِ والتَّثْبِيتِ، كَما فَعَلَ قَوْمُ طالُوتَ فَقالُوا: ﴿رَبَّنا أفْرِغْ عَلَيْنا صَبْرًا وثَبِّتْ أقْدامَنا وانْصُرْنا عَلى القَوْمِ الكافِرِينَ﴾ (Our Lord, pour upon us patience, plant firmly our feet, and give us victory over the disbelieving people) [al-Baqara: 250]. وقِيلَ: هم لا يُنْصَرُونَ، وكانَ هَذا شِعارَ المُؤْمِنِينَ عِنْدَ اللِّقاءِ، وقالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ كَعْبٍ: لَوْ رُخِّصَ تَرْكُ الذِّكْرِ لَرُخِّصَ في الحَرْبِ ولَذَكَرْنا حَيْثُ أُمِرَ بِالصَّمْتِ، ثُمَّ قِيلَ لَهُ: ﴿واذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ (And remember your Lord much) [Āl ʿImrān: 41]، وحُكْمُ هَذا الذِّكْرِ أنْ يَكُونَ خَفِيًّا، إلّا إنْ كانَ مِنَ الجَمِيعِ وقْتَ الحَمْلَةِ فَحَسَنٌ رَفْعُ الصَّوْتِ بِهِ؛ لِأنَّهُ يَفُتُّ في أعْضادِ الكُفّارِ، وفي سُنَنِ أبِي داوُدَ (Sunan Abi Dawud): «كانَ أصْحابُ الرَّسُولِ ﷺ يَكْرَهُونَ الصَّوْتَ عِنْدَ القِتالِ وعِنْدَ الجِنازَةِ»، وقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: يُكْرَهُ التَّلَثُّمُ عِنْدَ القِتالِ.

﴿وأطِيعُوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ ولا تَنازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا وتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكم واصْبِرُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصّابِرِينَ﴾ (And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute lest you lose courage and your strength depart, and be patient; indeed, Allah is with the patient). أمَرَهم تَعالى بِالطّاعَةِ لِلَّهِ ولِرَسُولِهِ، ونَهاهم عَنِ التَّنازُعِ وهو تَجاذُبُ الآراءِ وافْتِراقُها، والأظْهَرُ أنْ يَكُونَ فَتَفْشَلُوا جَوابًا لِلنَّهْيِ، فَهو مَنصُوبٌ، ولِذَلِكَ عُطِفَ عَلَيْهِ مَنصُوبٌ؛ لِأنَّهُ يَتَسَبَّبُ عَنِ التَّنازُعِ الفَشَلُ، وهو الخَوَرُ والجُبْنُ عَنْ لِقاءِ العَدُوِّ، وذَهابُ الدَّوْلَةِ بِاسْتِيلاءِ العَدُوِّ، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ فَتَفْشَلُوا مَجْزُومًا عَطْفًا عَلى ولا تَنازَعُوا، وذَلِكَ في قِراءَةِ عِيسى بْنِ عُمَرَ: ويَذْهَبْ، بِالياءِ وجَزْمِ الباءِ، وقَرَأ أبُو حَيْوَةَ وأبانٌ وعِصْمَةُ عَنْ عاصِمٍ: ويَذْهَبَ، بِالياءِ ونَصْبِ الباءِ، وقَرَأ الحَسَنُ وإبْراهِيمُ: ﴿فَتَفْشَلُوا﴾، بِكَسْرِ الشِّينِ، قالَ أبُو حاتِمٍ: وهَذا غَيْرُ مَعْرُوفٍ، وقالَ غَيْرُهُ: هي لُغَةٌ. قالَ مُجاهِدٌ: الرِّيحُ: النُّصْرَةُ والقُوَّةُ، وذَهَبَتْ رِيحُ أصْحابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ حِينَ ناغَوْهُ بِأُحُدٍ، وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: والرِّيحُ الدَّوْلَةُ، شُبِّهَتْ لِنُفُوذِ أمْرِها، وتَشْبِيهٌ بِالرِّيحِ وهُبُوبِها، فَقِيلَ: هَبَّتْ رِياحُ فُلانٍ، إذا دالَتْ لَهُ الدَّوْلَةُ ونَفَذَ أمْرُهُ. ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ:
؎أتَنْظُرانِ قَلِيلًا رَيْثَ غَفْلَتِهِمْ ∗∗∗ أمْ تَعْدُوانِ فَإنَّ الرِّيحَ لِلْعادِي
انْتَهى، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي عُبَيْدَةَ: إنَّ الرِّيحَ هي الدَّوْلَةُ، ومِنِ اسْتِعارَةِ الرِّيحِ قَوْلُ الآخَرِ:
؎إذا هَبَّتْ رِياحُكَ فاغْتَنِمْها ∗∗∗ فَإنَّ لِكُلِّ عاصِفَةٍ سُكُونا
ورَواهُ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: رُكُودًا. وقالَ شاعِرُ الأنْصارِ:(p-٥٠٤)
؎قَدْ عَوَّدَتْهم صِباهم أنْ يَكُونَ لَهم ∗∗∗ رِيحُ القِتالِ وأسْلابُ الَّذِينَ لَقُوا
وقالَ زَيْدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: ويَذْهَبَ رِيحُكم مَعْناهُ الرُّعْبُ مِن قُلُوبِ عَدُوِّكم، ومِنهُ قِيلَ لِلْخائِفِ: انْتَفَخَ سَحْرُهُ. قالَ ابْنُ عَطِيَّةَ: وهَذا حَسَنٌ بِشَرْطِ أنْ يَعْلَمَ العَدُوُّ بِالتَّنازُعِ، فَإذا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ فالذّاهِبُ قُوَّةُ المُتَنازِعِينَ فَيَنْهَزِمُونَ، انْتَهى، وقالَ ابْنُ زَيْدٍ وغَيْرُهُ الرِّيحُ عَلى بابِها، ورُوِيَ في ذَلِكَ أنَّ النَّصْرَ لَمْ يَكُنْ قَطُّ إلّا بِرِيحٍ تَهُبُّ فَتَضْرِبُ في وُجُوهِ الكُفّارِ، واسْتَنَدَ بَعْضُهم في هَذِهِ المَقالَةِ إلى قَوْلِهِ: نُصِرْتُ بِالصَّبا، وقالَ الحَكَمُ: وتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكم، يَعْنِي الصَّبا؛ إذْ بِها نُصِرَ مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ وأُمَّتُهُ، وقالَ مُقاتِلٌ: رِيحُكم حِدَّتُكم، وقالَ عَطاءٌ: جَلَدُكم، وحَكى التَّبْرِيزِيُّ: هَيْبَتُكم، ومِنهُ قَوْلُ الشّاعِرِ:
؎كَما حَمَيْناكَ يَوْمَ النَّعْفِ مِن شَطَطِ ∗∗∗ والفَضْلُ لِلْقَوْمِ مِن رِيحٍ ومِن عَدَدِ

﴿ولا تَكُونُوا كالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيارِهِمْ بَطَرًا ورِئاءَ النّاسِ ويَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ واللَّهُ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ﴾ (And do not be like those who went out from their homes insolently and to be seen by people, and who turn others from the way of Allah; and Allah encompasses what they do). نَزَلَتْ في أبِي جَهْلٍ وأصْحابِهِ خَرَجُوا لِنُصْرَةِ العِيرِ بِالقَيْناتِ والمَعازِفِ، ووَرَدُوا الجَحْفَةَ فَبَعَثَ خِفافٌ الكِنانِيُّ - وكانَ صَدِيقًا لَهُ - بِهَدايا مَعَ ابْنِهِ، وقالَ: إنْ شِئْتَ أمْدَدْناكَ بِالرِّجالِ، وإنْ شِئْتَ بِنَفْسِي مَعَ مَن خَفَّ مِن قَوْمِي، فَقالَ أبُو جَهْلٍ: إنْ كُنّا نُقاتِلُ اللَّهَ، كَما يَزْعُمُ مُحَمَّدٌ فَواللَّهِ ما لَنا بِاللَّهِ طاقَةٌ، وإنْ كُنّا نُقاتِلُ النّاسَ فَواللَّهِ إنَّ بِنا عَلى النّاسِ لَقُوَّةً، واللَّهِ لا نَرْجِعُ عَنْ قِتالِ مُحَمَّدٍ حَتّى نَرِدَ بَدْرًا فَنَشْرَبَ فِيها الخُمُورَ وتَعْزِفَ عَلَيْنا القَيْناتُ، فَإنَّ بَدْرًا مَرْكَزٌ مِن مَراكِزِ العَرَبِ وسُوقٌ مِن أسْواقِهِمْ، حَتّى تَسْمَعَ العَرَبُ مَخْرَجَنا فَتَهابَنا آخِرَ الأبَدِ، فَوَرَدُوا بَدْرًا فَسُقُوا كُؤُوسَ المَنايا مَكانَ الخَمْرِ، وناحَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ النَّوائِحُ مَكانَ القَيْناتِ، فَنَهى اللَّهُ المُؤْمِنِينَ أنْ يَكُونَ مِثْلَ هَؤُلاءِ بَطِرِينَ طَرِبِينَ مُرائِينَ بِأعْمالِهِمْ صادِّينَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، وقالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «اللَّهُمَّ إنَّ قُرَيْشًا أقْبَلَتْ بِفَخْرِها وخُيَلائِها تُجادِلُ وتُكَذِّبُ رَسُولَكَ، اللَّهُمَّ فَأحْنِها الغَداةَ»، وفي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿واللَّهُ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ﴾ وعِيدٌ وتَهْدِيدٌ لِمَن بَقِيَ مِنَ الكُفّارِ.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on Surah 8, verses 41–47 (part 1 of 4):**

﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, a fifth of it belongs to Allah, to the Messenger, to the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, if you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met. And Allah is capable of everything.﴾ ﴿When you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side, and the caravan was below you. Had you made an appointment together, you would surely have differed about the appointment. But Allah accomplished a matter that was destined to be done, so that whoever perished might perish by clear evidence, and whoever lived might live by clear evidence. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few. Had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart and disputed about the matter, but Allah saved you. Indeed, He knows what is in the breasts.﴾ ﴿And when He showed them to you as few when you met them, and made you appear few in their eyes, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was destined to be done. And to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may prosper.﴾ ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose heart and your strength depart. And be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾ ﴿And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people, and who bar from the way of Allah. And Allah encompasses what they do.﴾ ﴿And when Satan made their deeds appear fair to them and said, "No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector." But when the two hosts sighted each other, he turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment."﴾ [Al-Anfal: 48] ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "Their religion has deluded these people." But whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 49] ﴿If only you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs, "Taste the punishment of the burning.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 50] ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forth, and because Allah is never unjust to the servants.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 51] ﴿Like the practice of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is Strong and severe in punishment.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 52] ﴿That is because Allah never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves. And indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 53] ﴿Like the practice of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins and drowned the people of Pharaoh. And all of them were wrongdoers.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 54] ﴿Indeed, the worst of creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, for they will not believe.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 55] ﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear Allah.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 56] ﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war, then scatter those behind them, that they may take heed.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 57] ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 58] ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think they have escaped. Indeed, they cannot overcome.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 59] ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power and of horses stationed at the frontier, to strike terror into the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others besides them whom you do not know but Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 60] ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it also, and rely upon Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 61] ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed Allah is sufficient for you. It is He who strengthened you with His help and with the believers.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 62] ﴿And He joined their hearts together. Even if you had spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts, but Allah joined them. Indeed, He is Almighty, All-Wise.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 63] ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you, and so are the believers who follow you.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 64] ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 65] ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, knowing that there is weakness among you. So if there are a hundred steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand among you, they will overcome two thousand by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 66] ﴿It is not for a Prophet to take captives until he has thoroughly subdued the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 67]

(p-496) *al-Quṣuww* means distance, and *al-Quṣwā* is the feminine of *al-Aqṣā* (the farthest). Most of the morphologists (ahl al-taṣrīf) made distinctions regarding *fu'lā* forms whose third radical is a *wāw*. They said: if it is a noun (ism), the *wāw* is changed into a *yā'*, and they cite as examples what is an adjective (ṣifa), such as *al-Dunyā* (the world), *al-ʿUlyā* (the high), and *al-Quṣyā*. If it is an adjective, it remains, such as *al-Ḥulwā*, the feminine of *al-Aḥlā* (the sweeter). For this reason they said that *al-Quṣwā* with a *wāw* is anomalous (shādhdh), and that it is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, while *al-Quṣyā* is the dialect of Tamīm. Some grammarians held that if it is a noun the *wāw* remains, such as *Ḥuzwā* (a place name), and if it is an adjective it is changed, such as *al-Dunyā* and *al-ʿUlyā*. The retention of the *wāw* in an adjective is anomalous, as in *al-Ḥulwā*. Ibn al-Sikkīt explicitly stated that *al-Quṣwā* is rare. Al-Zamakhsharī said: As for *al-Quṣwā*, it is like *al-Qawad* in retaining the original form. *Al-Quṣyā* has also come, but the usage of *al-Quṣwā* is more common, just as *istaṣwaba* (he deemed correct) is more common than *istaṣāba*, and *ughīlat* is used alongside *aghālat*. The preference between the two positions is mentioned in grammar works.

*Al-Baṭar*: Al-Harawī said: it is tyranny at the time of blessing. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: poor endurance of error. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: bewilderment in the face of truth, so one does not see it as truth. Al-Zajjāj said: one is arrogant toward the truth and so does not accept it. Al-Kisāʾī said: it derives from the Arabs' saying *dhahaba damuhu baṭaran*, meaning "his blood was wasted in vain." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: *al-baṭar* is insolence, ingratitude for blessings, and being occupied with exultation in them, away from giving thanks for them.

*Nakaṣa*: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: he returned backward in flight. Others said: this is its original meaning, and then it was used for returning from the place one came from. The poet said:

> They strike the sword blades when they meet, they do not turn back when they are pressed in battle, and they defend.

It is said: he intended a matter, then turned back from it. Ta'abbaṭa Sharran said:

> Turning back upon one's heels is not a noble act; indeed, nobility is advancing upon the spear.

Here there is no *qahqarā* (backward retreat); rather it is flight. Mu'arrij said: *nakaṣa* means "returned," in the dialect of Sulaym.

*Sharrada*: it means scattered and drove away. *Al-musharrad* means the dispersed, the expelled. As for *sharradha* with a *dhāl*, it will come, God willing, when mention is made of the reading of those who read with a *dhāl*.

*Al-taḥrīḍ* is intensive urging in incitement. *Ḥarrakahu*, *ḥarrasahu*, and *ḥarraḍahu* have the same meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī said: it derives from *ḥaraḍ*, which is when illness wears a person down and he is so afflicted that he nearly dies; or it is that one calls him *ḥaraḍ* and says to him, "I only see you as ḥaraḍ (wasted) in this matter and sick with it," in order to stir and move him to it. A group said: the meaning is "urge them to fight until it becomes clear to you which of them has abandoned it, that he is *ḥāriḍ*." Al-Naqqāsh said: this is a statement that is neither coherent nor necessarily implied by the wording. Al-Zajjāj leaned toward it. *Al-ḥāriḍ*, the one close to destruction, is a word distinct from this one and has nothing to do with it. *Athkhanathu al-jirāḥāt* means the wounds made him heavy so that movement became difficult for him. *Athkhanahu al-maraḍ* means illness made him heavy, from *al-thakhāna*, which is thickness and density. *Al-ikhkhān* is exaggeration in killing and wounding.

* *

﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, a fifth of it belongs to Allah, to the Messenger, to the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, if you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met. And Allah is capable of everything.﴾ Al-Kalbī said: it was revealed at Badr. Al-Wāqidī said: the *khums* (one-fifth division) was in the expedition of Banū Qaynuqāʿ, a month and three days after Badr, on the half of Shawwāl, at the twentieth month after the Hijra. The connection of this verse to what precedes it is that when Allah commanded fighting the disbelievers so that there would be no *fitna* (persecution/discord), this required battles and wars. So He mentioned some rulings concerning the spoils, and in this there was good news for the believers of their victory over the disbelievers, and the division of what was obtained from them of spoils. The address in *wa-ʿlamū* ("and know") is to the believers. *Al-ghanīma* (spoils) in common usage is what the Muslims obtain from the enemy through effort; its origin is gaining something. It is said: *ghanima ghanman*. The poet said:

> I have wandered through the horizons until I was content with the spoils of returning home.

Another said:

> The one who feeds on plunder, on the day of plunder, his food is his; wherever he goes, and the one deprived is deprived.

The spoils of war (ghanimah) and the fay' (property gained without battle): are they synonymous or distinct? There are two opinions, and this will come up when the fay' is discussed, God willing. The apparent meaning is that whatever is taken as spoil is subject to the one-fifth levy (khums), whatever it is, so its fifth belongs to those whom God named. As for His words, ﴿Indeed, for God is a fifth of it﴾, the apparent meaning is that what is attributed to God is spent on acts of obedience, such as charity to the poor among the Muslims and the upkeep of the Ka'bah and similar things. A group held this view. It is also said that the fifth used to be divided into six parts, and the portion attributed to God was distributed among those we have mentioned. Abu al-'Aliyah said: God's share is spent on the door (ritaj) of the Ka'bah. He also reported that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would take the fifth, put his hand into it, take a handful and set it aside for the Ka'bah, and this was God's share; then he would divide the rest into five parts. It is also said that God's share goes to the public treasury (bayt al-mal).

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Nakha'i, Qatadah and al-Shafi'i said: His words ﴿Indeed, for God is a fifth of it﴾ are an opening phrase (istiftah kalam), as a man says to his slave: "May God free you, and I free you," for the sake of blessing and magnifying the matter. The whole world belongs to God, and God's share and the Messenger's share are one. The Messenger (ﷺ) would divide the fifth into five parts. This is the view al-Zamakhshari cited as a possibility. He said: It may be that the meaning of ﴿for God and for the Messenger﴾ (Al-Anfal: 24) is like His words: ﴿God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ (At-Tawbah: 62). And the meaning of His words ﴿Indeed, for God is a fifth of it﴾ may be: it is part of the right of the fifth that it be offered as a means of drawing near to Him alone. Then He singled out these five from among the ways of drawing near, giving them precedence over others, as in His words: ﴿Gabriel and Michael﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 98). The apparent meaning is that the Messenger, peace be upon him, has a share of the fifth.

Ibn 'Abbas said, as al-Tabari reported: God and the Messenger have no share; his share is for his kinsfolk. The fifth is divided into four parts. A group said: it is returned to the four-fifths. 'Ali said: the imam takes the share of God and His Messenger. The apparent meaning is that he, peace be upon him, had no share of the spoils except one share.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: He, peace be upon him, was specially privileged in three respects regarding the spoils: he had a fifth of the fifth; he had a man's share in the remaining four-fifths; and he had the safi, which he took before the spoils were divided, a mount, a sword, or a female slave. No one after him has a safi, by consensus, except what Abu Thawr said, that the safi belongs to the imam. This is an opinion counted among the anomalous views. End of quote.

A group said: the Messenger (ﷺ) did not leave an inheritance, so his share lapsed. It is also said that his share is held in trust for his kinsfolk, and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz sent it to them. A group said: it belongs to the kinsfolk of the one who holds authority after him. al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it was for the Messenger (ﷺ) during his lifetime, and when he died it was given to the custodian of affairs (wali al-amr) after him. End of quote.

Dhu al-qurba (the kinsfolk) means the kinsfolk of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The apparent meaning is the general sense of his kin. A group said: all of Quraysh are kinsfolk. Abu Hanifah and al-Shafi'i said: they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, who deserve it because of support and assistance, not the Banu 'Abd Shams or the Banu Nawfal. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, 'Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and Ibn 'Abbas said: they are only the Banu Hashim. Mujahid said: the family of Muhammad were not permitted to receive charity, so a share of the fifth was given to them. Ibn 'Abbas said: but our people refused this for us and said: all of Quraysh are kinsfolk. The apparent meaning is that this share remains for the kinsfolk, and that it belongs to both their rich and their poor. Ibn 'Abbas said: it was divided into six: for God and the Messenger two shares, and one share for his relatives, until he died. Then Abu Bakr divided the fifth into three parts, and this was also narrated from 'Umar and those who came after him among the caliphs. It is also reported that Abu Bakr withheld the fifth from the Banu Hashim and said: What is due to you is that your poor be given, your unmarried women be married, and whoever among you has no servant be provided with one. As for your wealthy, they are in the position of the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil); the wealthy person is not given anything from charity, nor is a wealthy orphan. It is reported from Zayd ibn 'Ali: it is not permitted for us to build palaces from it, nor to ride fine horses from it.

Some said: the share of the kinsfolk belongs to the kinsfolk of the caliph. The apparent meaning is that the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer are general terms covering the orphans and needy of the Muslims, and the wayfarer is among them. It is also said that the entire fifth belongs to the kinsfolk. It was said to 'Ali: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and the orphans and the needy﴾. He said: our orphans and our needy. It is reported from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali that they said: the whole verse concerns Quraysh and its needy. The apparent sense of the conjunction requires that the shares be shared equally, so that no one is deprived. This is what al-Shafi'i said, and he said: the imam may give preference to those in greater need, but he must not deprive any category of them. Malik said: the imam may give to the neediest and deprive the others of the categories.

The verse does not address who spends the four-fifths. The apparent meaning is that it is not divided among one who did not take part in the gain. If reinforcements join the fighters before the spoils have been brought into the territory of Islam, then according to Abu Hanifah they are partners with them in it. Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, al-Layth and al-Shafi'i said: they do not share with them.

The apparent meaning is that whoever gains something and fights alone, without the imam's permission, has his gain subject to the fifth. This is the view of al-Thawri and al-Shafi'i. The companions of Abu Hanifah said: it belongs to him alone and is not subject to the fifth. Some of them made a distinction on this. al-Awza'i said: if the imam wishes, he may punish him and deprive him; and if he wishes, he may take the fifth and the rest belongs to him.

The apparent meaning is that His words ﴿that whatever you gain﴾ are addressed to the believers. So no share is given to an unbeliever who attended with the imam's permission and fought. The Muslim slaves are included in the address, so what they gain belongs to their masters. al-Thawri and al-Awza'i said: if the protected non-Muslims (ahl al-dhimmah) are enlisted, they are given a share. Ashhab said: if a man in chains (al-muqayyad) or a dhimmi leaves the army and they gain something, the spoils belong to the army and not to them.

The apparent meaning is that His words ﴿that whatever you gain of anything, indeed for God is a fifth of it﴾ are general, covering everything gained: animals, goods, minerals, land and other things. So all of that is subject to the fifth. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, except for adult men. He said: the imam has the choice regarding them between releasing them as a favour, killing them, or taking them captive. Whoever is taken captive among them is subject to the rule of spoils. Malik said: if the imam sees fit to divide the land, that is correct; or if his judgment leads him not to divide it, he does not divide it.

The apparent meaning is that he takes nothing from the spoils other than the fifth. So the spoils of a slain enemy (salab al-maqtul) are general spoils and are not exclusively for the slayer, unless the commander assigns them to him for killing. This is the view of Malik, Abu Hanifah and al-Thawri. al-Awza'i, al-Layth, al-Shafi'i, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, Abu 'Ubayd, al-Tabari and Ibn al-Mundhir said: the spoils belong to the slayer. Ibn Surayj said: they agreed that whoever kills a captive, a woman, an old man, or finishes off a wounded man, or kills someone whose hands and feet have been cut off, or a fleeing man who poses no threat in his flight, like a bound man, has no right to the spoils of any of these. The disagreement is whether it is a condition that the slayer must be facing the slain and in the battle line, or whether this is not a condition. The evidence for these questions is fully treated in the books of jurisprudence, in the books on points of disagreement, and in the books on the rulings of the Qur'an.

The apparent meaning is that ma is a relative pronoun meaning "that which," and it is the subject of anna. Anna is written joined to ma, though by analogy it should be written separately, as they wrote ﴿Indeed what you are promised is coming﴾ (Al-An'am: 134) separately. The predicate of anna is His words ﴿indeed for God is a fifth of it﴾. The phrase anna li-llahi is in the nominative position as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "So the ruling is that for God..." The fa' (then) has entered this clause which functions as the predicate of anna, just as it entered the predicate of anna in His words: ﴿Indeed those who persecuted the believing men and women and then did not repent, for them is the punishment of hellfire﴾ (Al-Buruj: 10).

al-Zamakhshari said: fa-anna li-llahi is a subject whose predicate is omitted, its estimated form being: "a truth" or "a duty": "indeed for God is a fifth of it." End of quote. This second estimate, "or a duty that indeed for God is a fifth of it," makes anna and its two complements the subject of an omitted predicate, which is His words "a duty."

al-Farra' permitted ma to be conditional and governed by ghanimtum, with the subject of anna being an omitted pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n), its estimated form being innahu. The omission of this pronoun with the heavy anna is, according to Sibawayh, restricted to poetry.

al-Ju'fi reported from Harun from Abu 'Amr: fa-inna li-llahi with a kasrah on the hamzah. Ibn 'Atiyyah reported it from al-Ju'fi from Abu Bakr from 'Asim. This reading is strengthened by the reading of al-Nakha'i: fa-li-llahi khumusahu. al-Hasan and 'Abd al-Warith from Abu 'Amr read khumsahu with a sukun on the mim. al-Nakha'i read khimsahu with a kasrah on the kha', by assimilation (ittiba'), meaning the kha' takes the vowel of what precedes it, as in the reading of one who read (wa-al-sama'i dhati al-hubuk) with a kasrah on the ha', assimilating to the vowel of the ta', disregarding the sakin because it is a weak unprotected sakin.

Consider how fine this construction is: He made the existence of the fifth belong to God alone, and separated His name from the conjunctions by the phrase khumusahu, to make clear that God alone has the entitlement to the fifth. Then He conjoined the others with Him in a subordinate way. The construction could have been: fa-inna li-llahi wa-li-l-rasuli wa-li-dhi al-qurba wa-al-yatama wa-al-masakin wa-ibn al-sabil khumusahu, but it did not come that way.

The conditional's answer is omitted, its estimated form being: if you have believed in God, then know that the fifth of the spoils must be offered as a means of drawing near. Mere knowledge is not meant, but knowledge together with acting upon its requirement. For this reason some estimated: if you have believed in God, then accept what you were commanded regarding the spoils. Whoever held that the condition is connected in meaning to His words ﴿the best Protector and the best Helper﴾ (Al-Anfal: 40) is far off, the estimate being: "then know that God is your protector," with "and what We sent down" conjoined to "in God".

The Day of Discrimination (yawm al-furqan) is the Day of Badr, without disagreement. On it truth was distinguished from falsehood. The two hosts (al-jam'an) are the host of the believers and the host of the unbelievers. In it the chieftains of Quraysh were killed, as stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Miqsam, al-Hasan and Qatadah. It took place on Friday, the seventeenth of Ramadan in the second year after the Hijrah. This is the view of the majority. Abu Salih said it was on the nineteenth day.

What was sent down (al-munzal) refers to the signs, the angels and the victory. He concluded with an attribute of power, because God, exalted is He, granted the believers, though few, victory over the unbelievers, though many, on that day.

Zayd ibn 'Ali read 'ubudina with two dammahs, like the reading of the one who read wa-'ubud al-taghut with two dammahs. According to the reading 'abdina, it refers to the Messenger (ﷺ); according to 'ubudina, it refers to the Messenger and those believers with him.

The accusative of (yawm al-furqan) is that it is an adverbial complement governed by His words (wa-ma anzalna). al-Zajjaj said: it may also be governed by ghanimtum, meaning: that whatever you gained on the Day of Discrimination, the day the two hosts met, then indeed for such-and-such is its fifth; that is, if you have believed in God, so submit to that and comply. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: this interpretation is good in meaning, but there is an objection: it separates the adverb from what it depends on by this long stretch of speech. End of quote.

What al-Zajjaj said is not permissible. If ma is conditional, according to al-Farra's analysis, then the separation of the verb of the condition from its object by the answer clause and its dependents is required. If ma is relative, then it is not permissible to separate the verb of the relative clause from its object by the predicate of anna.

﴿When you were on the near bank of the valley and they were on the far bank, and the caravan was lower than you﴾. al-'Udwah is the bank of the valley; it is also called shafir and daffah. It was named so because it prevents the water in the valley from passing beyond it, that is, it holds it back. The poet said:

"The rushing torrents kept me from visiting her,
and she said: behind her is a fierce, shifting war."

(p. 500) The open plain running alongside the valley is called *'udwa* (the near bank), because it is adjacent to the valley. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read *bil-'idwati* with a kasra on the ʿayn in both occurrences. The rest of the Seven Readers read it with a damma, while al-Hasan, Qatadah, Zayd ibn 'Ali and 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd read it with a fatha. Abu 'Amr denied the damma. Al-Akhfash said that only the kasra has been heard from the Arabs. Abu 'Ubayd said the damma is the most common of the three. Al-Yazidi said the kasra is the dialect of the Hijaz. It is possible that all three are dialectal variants. It is also possible that the fatha is a verbal noun that was used as a name. A line of Aws is also transmitted with both the kasra and the damma:

"A horseman who did not hold his bank today; they turned and fled swiftly, and had no intention of advancing."

It was also read *bil-'idyati*, with the waw changed to a ya' because of the kasra on the ʿayn. They did not count the unvowelled letter as a barrier, because it is a weak barrier. They did the same in *sibyatin*, *qinyatin* and *dinya*, as in their saying, "He is my cousin *dinya*." The basic form in this is the uncorrected one, as in *al-sifwa*, *al-dhirwa* and *al-rib'a*. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud the text is *bil-'udwati al-'ulya* (the upper bank) and *wa-hum bil-'udwati al-sufla* (the lower bank). The valley of Badr, for those facing east and the qibla, lies toward the sea, which is near that region. Al-Madina is in the valley, from the place of the battle, in the east, and the distance between them is two stages of travel. Zayd ibn 'Ali read *al-qusya*, and we have already mentioned that this is the analogical form. It is the dialect of Tamim.

The better view is that *wa-hum* and *wal-rakb* are conjoined to *antum* (you). They are then introductory subjects that divide the description of their state and the state of their enemies. It is also possible that the two waws are the waw of the circumstantial clause (*wawa al-hal*). *Asfala* is an adverbial of place in the position of the predicate. Zayd ibn 'Ali read *asfalu* with a damma, extending the adverb so that it became the subject itself, by metaphor. *Al-rakb* (the caravan) are the forty men who were leading the caravan of Abu Sufyan. It is said they were the camels carrying the provisions and goods of the unbelievers, which were in a place they felt safe.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask, what is the benefit of this specification, and of mentioning the positions of the two groups, and that the caravan was lower than them? I say: the benefit is to inform about a state that indicates the strength of the enemy's position and its might, the completeness of its numbers, and the ready means of victory for it. It also shows the weakness of the Muslims' position and the scattering of their affairs. It shows that their victory in such a state was nothing but a work of God, Exalted, and a proof that this matter could not have been accomplished except by His power, His might and His overwhelming ability. The far bank, where the polytheists encamped, had water and was good ground. There was no water on the near bank; it was soft ground, where the feet sink, and one could not walk there except with exhaustion and hardship. The caravan was behind the backs of the enemy, despite their large numbers. Protecting it strengthened their zeal and sharpened their intentions in fighting for it. For this reason the Arabs used to go out to war with their women and wealth, so that the defence of the sanctities and their jealousy for them would move them to exert their utmost effort in battle, so that they would not leave behind them anything they might think of withdrawing to. This gathers their hearts, controls their resolve, settles their souls on not leaving their positions and not abandoning their stations, and on spending the utmost of their valour and the extreme of their strength. In it is a depiction of what God, Glorified is He, arranged regarding the affair of the battle of Badr." End of quotation. It is an excellent statement.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "The caravan and the one who managed its affair, Abu Sufyan, had turned aside from Badr when he learned of the Prophet ﷺ, and took the route of the sea. So it was lower in relation to the upper part of the valley from where [the Prophet's army] came."

﴿And if you had made an appointment with one another, you would have differed about the appointment; but [it was so] that God might accomplish a matter that was to be done, so that whoever perished might perish by clear proof, and whoever lived might live by clear proof. Indeed God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

The meeting took place without an appointment. Mujahid said: "Abu Sufyan and his companions came from Syria as merchants, and they did not perceive the companions of Badr. The companions of Muhammad ﷺ did not perceive the unbelievers of Quraysh, nor did the unbelievers of Quraysh perceive Muhammad ﷺ and his companions, until they met at the water of Badr, all of them to draw water, and they fought. The companions of Muhammad ﷺ overcame them and took them captive." Al-Tabari and others said: the meaning is, if you had agreed on a meeting in order to gather, then had known their numbers and your own scarcity, you would have differed and not gathered with them. Al-Zamakhshari said the same. He said: "If you and the people of Mecca had made an appointment and agreed among yourselves on a time to meet for battle, some of you would have feared others. Your scarcity and their abundance would have deterred you from keeping the appointment, and what was in their hearts of awe of the Messenger of God ﷺ and the Muslims would have deterred them too. So there would not have come about for you the meeting that God had enabled and arranged for." Al-Mahdawi said: the meaning is that you would have differed because of the hindrances and obstacles that block people.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "This is nobler than the view of al-Tabari, and sounder." Its explanation is that the purpose of the verse is to make clear God's blessing and power in the story of Badr and His facilitating of what was facilitated of it. So the meaning is: when God prepared this situation for you, if you had made an appointment for it, you would have differed, except with God's facilitation, which completed it. This is like when you say to your companion about a matter God willed without much effort: "If we had persisted in this and striven for it, it would not have been accomplished like this."

(p. 501) Al-Kirmani said: "If you and the polytheists had made an appointment for fighting, you would have differed about the appointment, meaning they would not have believed in your agreement, seeking to catch you unawares and to trick you." It is also said: the meaning is, if you had made an appointment apart from God's decree regarding the matter of war, you would have differed about the appointment, because when God does not decree a matter it does not happen. End of quotation.

﴿But [it was so] that God might accomplish﴾: but you met without an appointment, so that God might accomplish a matter of the victory of His religion, the exaltation of His word, and the breaking and humiliation of the unbelievers, which was to be done, meaning established, realised and occurring. He expressed it with *maf'ulan* (to be done) to affirm that it would certainly happen. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "[God] accomplishes a matter which He had decreed in eternity as something to be done for you, on condition that you exist at the time of its existence. All of this is known to Him." Al-Zamakhshari said: *li-yaqdiya Allah* is connected to a deleted element, meaning: so that God might accomplish a matter that had to be done, namely the granting of victory to His friends and the subjugation of His enemies. He arranged this. It is also said: *kana* here means *sara* (became). *Li-yuhlika* is a substitute for *li-yaqdiya*, so it is connected to what *li-yaqdiya* is connected to. It is also said: it is connected to *maf'ulan*. It is also said: the original is *wa-li-yuhlika*, and the conjunction was deleted.

The apparent meaning is: that those among the unbelievers of Quraysh and others who were killed should be destroyed by a clear proof from God and a warning through the message, and that whoever lived should live by a clear proof from Him and a warning, with no argument against him. Ibn Ishaq and others said: *li-yakfura wa-yu'mina* (so that he who disbelieves may disbelieve and he who believes may believe). The meaning is that God, Exalted, made the story of Badr a lesson and a sign, so that whoever believed would believe on the basis of clarity and proof, and whoever disbelieved would disbelieve on the same basis.

Al-A'mash and 'Isma ibn Abi Bakr from 'Asim read *li-yahlika* with a fatha on the lam. Nafi', al-Bazzi and Abu Bakr read *man hayya* with *fakk* (separating the two identical letters), while the rest of the Seven read it with idgham (assimilation). Al-Mutalammis said:

"So this is the time of display, its sharp edge alive."

The separated and the assimilated forms are two well-known dialects. He concluded with these two attributes because disbelief and belief entail verbal utterance and inner conviction. So He is All-Hearing of your words and All-Knowing of your intentions.

﴿When God showed them to you in your dream as few. And had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart and disputed about the matter, but God saved [you]. Indeed He knows what is within the breasts.﴾

The address is to the Messenger ﷺ. The reports are consistent that it was a dream of sleep, in which the Messenger ﷺ saw the unbelievers as few. He informed his companions of it, and their souls were strengthened and they became bold against their enemies. When the Prophet ﷺ awoke he said to his companions: "Rejoice, for I saw the places where the people will fall." The meaning of "few" here is few in worth, weakness and valour, and that they would be defeated and slain. It is not to be taken as few in number, because his dream was true. He knew that they were between nine hundred and a thousand, so it is not possible to interpret it as fewness of numbers.

It is reported from al-Hasan that the meaning of *fi manamika* (in your dream) is *fi 'aynika* (in your eye), because the eye is the place of sleep, just as a coverlet is called a *manama* because one sleeps in it. Thus the seeing would be in waking. On this basis al-Naqqash interpreted it, and he mentioned it from al-Mazini. But what is reported from al-Hasan is weak. Al-Zamakhshari said: "This is an interpretation with forced strain. I do not think the report from al-Hasan is sound, nor does it accord with his knowledge of the language of the Arabs and their eloquence. The meaning is: had He shown them to you as many in your dream, you would have lost heart, meaning you would have been cowardly and shrunk from the encounter, and you would have disputed about the matter, meaning your opinions would have been divided over the question of fighting. That would have been a cause of your defeat and of your not advancing against your enemies, for if he had seen them as many, he would have informed you of his vision, and you would have lost heart. Since the Messenger, peace be upon him, was protected from cowardice and preserved from defects, He attributed the cowardice to those in whom it is possible. So He, Exalted, said: 'you would have lost heart.' This is one of the excellences of the Qur'an. But God saved [you] from cowardice, dispute and disagreement by showing him the unbelievers as few, so he informed them of that, and their souls were strengthened by it. Indeed He knows what is within the breasts, knowing what will be in them of boldness and cowardice, patience and despair." (p. 502)

*Idh* (when) is a substitute for *idh* (the earlier one), and *qalilan* is in the accusative. Al-Zamakhshari said: "[*qalilan* is] a circumstantial accusative (*'ala al-hal*)." What he said is apparent, because *ara* (to show) is a causative form of *ra'a* in the sense of seeing with the eye. It takes two objects: the first is the *kaf* of address to the Messenger ﷺ, and the second is the pronoun for the unbelievers. Thus *qalilan* and *kathiran* are accusatives of circumstance. Some grammarians claimed that *ara* in the sense of seeing in a dream takes three objects, like *a'lama* (to inform), and they took this verse as an example: *idh yurikahum Allah fi manamika qalilan*. On this view, *qalilan* is a third object. But the permissibility of deleting this accusative on its own refutes this view. You say: "I saw Zayd in the sleep," and "God showed me Zayd in the sleep."

﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and made you appear few in their eyes, so that God might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to God all affairs are returned.﴾

This sight was in waking, not in sleep. He made the unbelievers appear few in the eyes of the believers, to belittle them and so that they would not be cowardly in meeting them. Ibn Mas'ud said: "They were made to seem few in our eyes, until I said to a man beside me: do you think they are seventy?" He said: "I think they are a hundred." This was from 'Abd Allah because he had not heard what the Messenger ﷺ was informed of regarding their number.

The believers were made to appear few in the eyes of the unbelievers, to the extent that one of them said: "They are only camel-eaters." This was before the encounter, so that they would be emboldened against the believers and the battle would begin and the fighting would engage. For if they had been numerous before the encounter, they would have held back and sought an escape, or prepared and sought help. When the fighting engaged, God made the believers appear numerous in the eyes of the unbelievers, so they were stunned, awed, their strength failed, and they saw what was not in their reckoning. This is as He said: ﴿They saw them as twice their number with their own eyes﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:13]. The greatest proof against them is the clarity of the sign: its smallness at first and its largeness at the end.

The seeing of each of the two groups by the other could be either because God concealed some of them from others, or because He created in their eyes what made them consider the many as few. This applies if the seeing is literal. If it is in the sense of estimation and the caution that people use, then it is possible. In either case, the Messenger does not fall under the address *idh yurikumuhum* (when He showed them to you), because it is not permissible that he should see the many as few, neither literally nor by estimation. It is possible that it is from the category of belittling the rank, awe and valour, not from the category of belittling the number. Do you not see the saying: "A man is many with his brother"? And the line of the poet:

"I go about and set out in folly, making many of him whom I have little of."

فَهَذا مِن بابِ التَّقْلِيلِ والتَّكْثِيرِ في المَنزِلَةِ والقَدْرِ، لا مِن بابِ تَقْلِيلِ العَدَدِ، لِيَقْضِيَ: أيْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ لِيَقْضِيَ، والمَفْعُولُ في الآيَتَيْنِ هو القِصَّةُ بِأسْرِها؛ وقِيلَ: هُما لِمَعْنَيَيْنِ مِن مَعانِي القِصَّةِ، أُرِيدَ بِالأوَّلِ الوَعْدُ بِالنُّصْرَةِ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ، وبِالثّانِي الِاسْتِمْرارُ عَلَيْها، وتَقَدَّمَ تَفْسِيرُ: ﴿وإلى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ﴾ واخْتِلافُ القُرّاءِ في (تُرْجَعُ) في سُورَةِ البَقَرَةِ.

﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً فاثْبُتُوا واذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا لَعَلَّكم تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ (O you who believe, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much, so that you may prosper). أيْ: فِئَةً كافِرَةً، حَذَفَ الوَصْفَ لِأنَّ المُؤْمِنِينَ ما كانُوا يَلْقَوْنَ إلّا الكُفّارَ، واللِّقاءُ اسْمٌ لِلْقِتالِ غالِبٌ، وأمَرَهم تَعالى بِالثَّباتِ وهو مُقَيَّدٌ بِآيَةِ الضَّعْفِ، وفي الحَدِيثِ (ḥadīth, a prophetic report): «لا تَتَمَنَّوْا لِقاءَ العَدُوِّ وسَلُوا اللَّهَ العافِيَةَ، فَإذا لَقِيتُمُوهم فاثْبُتُوا» . وأمَرَهم بِذِكْرِهِ تَعالى كَثِيرًا في هَذا المَوْطِنِ العَظِيمِ مِن (p-٥٠٣)مُصابَرَةِ العَدُوِّ والتَّلاحُمِ بِالرِّماحِ وبِالسُّيُوفِ، وهي حالَةٌ يَقَعُ فِيها الذُّهُولُ عَنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَأُمِرُوا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ؛ إذْ هو تَعالى الَّذِي يُفْزَعُ إلَيْهِ عِنْدَ الشَّدائِدِ ويُسْتَأْنَسُ بِذِكْرِهِ ويُسْتَنْصَرُ بِدُعائِهِ، ومَن كانَ كَثِيرَ التَّعَلُّقِ بِاللَّهِ ذَكَرَهُ في كُلِّ مَوْطِنٍ حَتّى في المَواضِعِ الَّتِي يُذْهَلُ فِيها عَنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ ويَغِيبُ فِيها الحِسُّ: ﴿ألا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ القُلُوبُ﴾ (Indeed, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest) [al-Ra'd: 28]. وحَكى لِي بَعْضُ الشُّجْعانِ أنَّهُ حالَةَ التِحامِ القِتالِ تَأْخُذُ الشُّجاعَ هِزَّةٌ وتَعْتَرِيهِ، مِثْلَ السُّكْرِ لِهَوْلِ المُلْتَقى، فَأمَرَ المُؤْمِنِينَ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ في هَذِهِ الحالَةِ العَظِيمَةِ، وقَدْ نَظَمَ الشُّعَراءُ هَذا المَعْنى فَذَكَرُوا أنَّهم في أشَقِّ الأوْقاتِ عَلَيْهِمْ وأشَدِّها لَمْ يَنْسَوْا مَحْبُوبَهم وأكْثَرُوا في ذَلِكَ، فَقالَ بَعْضُهم:
؎ذَكَرْتُ سُلَيْمى وحَرُّ الوَغى ∗∗∗ كَقَلْبِيَ ساعَةَ فارَقْتُها
؎وأبْصَرْتُ بَيْنَ القَنا قَدَّها ∗∗∗ وقَدْ مِلْنَ نَحْوِي فَعانَقْتُها
